transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because I'm having a major issue at work lately. I manage construction sites, and... every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or an upper platform now, my head just tells me I'm about to go right over the edge. 

It doesn't even make sense to me, because I can look right at it and see the rails are in place. I know the setup is supposed to be safe, but I just can't shake that feeling. It's getting really hard to do my job.
Does this fear happen only when you’re up high or near an edge?

Yeah, pretty much. It's... well, the second I step onto any temporary stairs, or even just walk toward an open upper floor, it hits me immediately. My chest tightens right up, my hands get all wet and sweaty, and... I just feel like my legs might lock up on me before I can even make myself take another step.
Have you ever had one of these sudden panic episodes when you were not near a height or an edge?

No, not at all. It's really just the heights. If I'm down on the ground level, or working in the site trailer, I'm completely fine. It's only when I have to go up. I don't get that feeling anywhere else.
